claims.text: The investigated particles are sub-5 nm AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles synthesized by pulsed laser deposition on a silicon nitride membrane.
The initial nanoparticles have elliptical or icosahedral geometries.
The nanoparticles initially possess a metastable FCC structure produced by kinetic trapping rather than thermodynamic equilibrium.
Surface-energy minimization overrides sluggish diffusion in sub-5 nm AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles.
The relevant thermal mechanism becomes dominant within an estimated heating range of 400–800 °C.
The mechanism becomes dominant when surface-to-volume effects exceed the entropic stabilization energy.
Local lattice distortion occurs at the nanoparticle surface and helps create preferential diffusion pathways.
Au and Cu are low-surface-energy species in this alloy and therefore preferentially diffuse to and enrich the nanoparticle surface.
Surface segregation of Au and Cu reduces the total Gibbs free energy by minimizing surface tension.
The surface-segregation driving force exceeds the diffusion activation-energy barrier and thereby negates sluggish diffusion.
Surface-enriched Au and Cu evaporate because they have lower cohesive energies under nanoconfinement.
Au and Cu loss increases rapidly and nonlinearly above the critical temperature.
Segregation and evaporation cause elliptical or icosahedral particles to become spherical.
Elemental evaporation widens the particle-size distribution and can ultimately cause particles to disappear.
Particle evaporation occurs before significant bulk coalescence or separation into distinct bulk phases.
The rate of elemental loss is inversely proportional to initial particle size.
The rate and critical temperature depend on the surface-energy anisotropy associated with an icosahedral versus truncated-octahedral initial shape.
Surface-energy control applies only below 10 nm and does not apply to particles above 20 nm, where bulk diffusion and entropic stabilization prevail.
High configurational entropy can stabilize a single-phase structure.
Sluggish diffusion prevents segregation and preserves the size and shape of AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles at high temperature.

contradictions.description: Falsification condition (3) says that failure of simulations without surface-energy gradients and success of simulations including those gradients would falsify the hypothesis. That result would instead support the stated surface-energy-gradient mechanism.
